expectations.text: Raises the factor score indeterminacy problem — EFA factor scores are not uniquely determined; multiple sets of scores are consistent with any given factor solution
expectations.evidence: The response dedicates an entire section ('The indeterminacy problem') to this: 'for any given factor solution — the same loadings, the same observed covariance matrix — there are infinitely many sets of factor scores that are mathematically consistent with the model.' Explicitly names factor score indeterminacy and cites Grice (2001).

expectations.text: Does not simply confirm 'yes, save fa()$scores and use them in regression' without addressing indeterminacy
expectations.evidence: Response opens with 'Not quite' and immediately flags the indeterminacy problem before giving any practical guidance. Never endorses the described workflow as-is.

expectations.text: Explains that EFA factor scores (unlike CFA latent variable scores) lack a unique mathematical solution
expectations.evidence: 'This is not a rounding issue or a sampling artifact. It's a logical consequence of the common factor model: the factors are latent (unobserved), and the observed items underdetermine them.' Contrasts with CFA: 'CFA in lavaan... produces factor scores that are better-defined than EFA scores because the model imposes additional constraints that reduce indeterminacy.'

expectations.text: Recommends alternatives: sum scores or unit-weighted composites of high-loading items as more transparent and reproducible
expectations.evidence: Option 1 explicitly recommends unit-weighted composite scores with code example, noting they are 'transparent, reproducible... don't require the factor model at all, and behave well in downstream regression.'

expectations.text: Optionally notes that CFA with lavaan allows better-defined factor score estimation if model fit is adequate
expectations.evidence: Option 2 explicitly covers CFA with lavaan: 'fit that structure as a CFA' using lavPredict(), noting that CFA scores have 'additional model constraints [that] sharply reduce indeterminacy compared to EFA.' Also mentions SEM as Option 3.

expectations.text: Does not treat fa()$scores as equivalent to true factor scores or latent variable scores
expectations.evidence: Explicitly states: 'The problem is interpreting those scores as if they are the unique, true latent factor scores. They aren't.' Clarifies fa()$scores is 'one arbitrary choice' from an infinite family of equivalent solutions.
